summary: The one Flask application every other feature runs inside: response headers on every response, the request gate that serves or refuses every request before any handler runs with a status taken from the Refusals table alone, the CSRF header check, the session cookie, the SQLite schema including the two administrator triggers, the vault and administration surface split, and the authenticated chrome.

read.role: the chrome this feature renders, top bar, nav, Update values, Lock and the administrator's stripped bar. No screen of its own
the boundary the surface split is the routing half of

csp.value: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'

cspIsInvariant.value: the policy does not vary by route. A route that would need a looser policy is a design change, not a local override

noXFrameOptions.value: no separate X-Frame-Options header is served. frame-ancestors 'none' in the CSP covers framing

hsts.value: includeSubDomains always, plus preload only once the deployment is internet-reachable on a fixed domain that has served the header stably for the required probation period. Not applicable to a LAN or VPN-only deployment

csrfScope.value: required on every endpoint that is not meant to be reached by navigation: every state-changing one and GET /api/export. Every endpoint that requires the header is under /api/, and every other route is exempt from it and answers only GET and HEAD

csrfOrdering.value: the header check is step 1 of the request gate, before authentication and routing. No API route is exempt, so the check needs no routing. A request without the header changes nothing

csrfExemptRule.value: exempt are the routes meant to be reached by navigation: the server-rendered shell pages and the static endpoint. An exemption is a named route, never a path pattern, so an endpoint added under an existing prefix cannot inherit one

staticExemption.value: the static endpoint is exempt because no subresource request carries a custom header. What it serves is public by construction: the design tokens, the client-side code, the vendored Alpine build and the app's icon

appIcon.value: every shell page and every error page declares <link rel="icon" href="<static>/icon.png" type="image/png">, a transparent 1x1 PNG served by the static endpoint. It is not a data: URL, because img-src 'self' blocks it

noFaviconRoute.value: there is no /favicon.ico route and no exemption for it, so the request gate refuses it like any invented path

apiAndPageRequests.value: a path under /api/ is an API request and any other path is a page request

refusalPicking.value: a refusal's status depends only on the namespace, the X-Solvent-Request header and the session, never on whether the path exists, its surface or its method, so a probe learns nothing it did not send. No valid session means no cookie, a badly signed one, or an expired or revoked session

unresolvedCountsAsInvented.value: an unknown path, a method the route does not answer (OPTIONS included) and an address the router would redirect (//admin) are refused as invented. Nothing answers Method Not Allowed and no refusal redirects

urlMap.value: the URL map sets merge_slashes = False and turns off automatic OPTIONS responses. Any other redirect or Method Not Allowed the router would raise is refused at step 4 of the gate

value: 1 Header: an API request without X-Solvent-Request: 1 is refused. No API route is exempt, so this needs no routing
2 Authentication: the session cookie is read and looked up
3 No session, API: an API request with no valid session is refused unless it resolved to a Public route
4 Unresolved: a request that did not resolve is refused
5 No session, page: a Public page is served. A vault navigation page is served and renders its own sign-in card. Any other page is refused
6 Surface: a route whose group the session's kind does not reach is refused

requestGateRule.value: every request passes the steps in order, before any handler runs. The first that refuses decides the response, at the status the Refusals table gives

refusalHeaders.value: a refusal carries only the headers every response carries (CSP and HSTS), and its body depends only on its status and namespace: no Set-Cookie, Allow or Location, and no header a route sets on its own response, such as Cache-Control: no-store or Referrer-Policy

noOptions.value: no route answers OPTIONS: automatic OPTIONS responses are turned off

noCors.value: no CORS headers are served, which is why a cross-origin preflight for the custom header fails

sessionRow.value: (id, token_hash, principal_id, issued_at, last_active_at). The row shape does not vary by kind and carries no kind column, which is read through principal_id. last_active_at is written on every authenticated request

sessionCookie.value: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, carrying only a random session token signed with the Flask SECRET_KEY. No key material of any kind rides in the cookie. A valid signature alone is not a session: the token must hash to a stored row

secretKeyStartupRule.value: the app refuses to start when SECRET_KEY is absent or empty rather than generating one, and the failure names the variable without printing any value

schemaOwnership.value: one place creates the schema and opens the SQLite file on its writable volume. Each table's columns are stated by the feature that owns them: records by record-api.md, principals and credentials and dek_wrappers by register.md, invites by admin-invites.md, sessions by architecture.md Application hardening

lastLoginAtNeverNull.value: principals.last_login_at is never null though the DDL declares it nullable, because NOT NULL in SQLite means rebuilding principals. Its one writer is issuing a session. On every start, in the transaction that creates the schema, any null last_login_at is set to that row's created_at. A no-op once nothing is null, so it needs no schema version

administratorTriggers.value: a BEFORE INSERT on records and a BEFORE INSERT on dek_wrappers, each resolving the row's principal and aborting when its kind is administrator. A SQLite CHECK cannot reach another table, which is why these are triggers

value: the static endpoint, the framework's own static route

publicRule.value: Public routes answer without a session, to anyone. Public lifts the session requirement and nothing else: a Public API route still requires X-Solvent-Request and keeps its own feature's checks and rate limits. Public is a list of named routes, never a path pattern, and names nothing at /admin or under /api/admin/

surfaceSharedRule.value: reached by both kinds with a valid session

surfaceVault.value: the record store, the rate lookup including GET /api/rates/symbols, export, import, /api/sessions, /api/auth/logout-all, DELETE /api/auth/account, /settings, /settings/dimensions and /settings/export-import, the dashboard, and every screen that renders vault data. An administrator gets Not Found, /settings included. A route that redirects a vault owner still answers an administrator Not Found

oneVaultShellPage.value: the vault surface is one shell page, /dashboard, carrying every screen behind the gate as in-page addresses, settings, dimensions and export and import included. /settings, /settings/dimensions and /settings/export-import remain routes on the vault surface, each redirecting to the view it names, because a second shell page would discard the in-memory keys and charge the derivation again

surfaceAdministration.value: the /admin shell page and every /api/admin/* endpoint, including ones no feature file has been written for yet. A vault owner gets Not Found

surfaceCheckPlacement.value: the surface check is step 6 of the request gate, which checks the group against the session once per request, so no endpoint repeats it. The other groups are placed by prefix: outside Public, everything under /api/admin/ is administration and everything else that touches a vault is vault. A route matching no group is unreachable

rootPath.value: resolves by kind, the Dashboard for a vault owner and the Admin area for an administrator. It is the only route that resolves to different content per kind. Without a session it sends the visitor to the Dashboard, whose sign-in card signs in both kinds

chromeByKind.value: vault owner: nav of Dashboard and Settings, Update values shown, right-hand control Lock, record and decryption layer loaded. Administrator: no nav entries at all, Update values absent rather than disabled, right-hand control Sign out, record and decryption layer not loaded. Both: the embedded KDF envelope and the Argon2id worker

navHasNoAdminOrHoldingsEntry.value: there is no Holdings entry and no Admin entry in either bar, in any state

contentMaxWidth.value: 1200px on the ground. Forms are 480px, and 900px covers the sweep, a recording's own screen and account detail

alpineBuild.value: the CSP-safe build. The standard build needs unsafe-eval for x- expressions, which would gut the CSP

apiNoHeader.condition: an API request lacks the X-Solvent-Request header, whether or not its path exists and whatever the session (spec/architecture.md#refusals)

apiHeaderNoValidSession.condition: an API request carries the header and no valid session, and is not a resolved Public route. An expired session reads as an absent one (spec/architecture.md#refusals)

apiHeaderValidSessionRefused.condition: an API request carries the header and a valid session and is refused: an unknown path, an unresolved method or address, or a route of the other kind's surface (spec/architecture.md#refusals)

pageRefusal.condition: every refusal of a page request, with or without the header and with or without a valid session, including /admin signed out or as a vault owner, /settings as an administrator, an invented page path and //admin (spec/architecture.md#refusals, spec/features/app-shell.md#acceptance-criteria)

unresolvedRequest.value: no Method Not Allowed and no redirect
unresolvedRequest.condition: a method a route does not answer and an address the router would redirect are refused as an invented address is

faviconIco.value: refused as an invented page path

unhandledFailure.condition: never a designed answer, and it must still carry CSP and HSTS (spec/features/app-shell.md#acceptance-criteria)

fixtures: one route of each response shape, a shell page, a JSON endpoint, an unknown path, and a handler stubbed to raise, for the header-parity assertion
one valid session, one expired session and no session at all, plus a vault owner session and an administrator session, for the four session states of the refusal fingerprint matrix

a route enumerator that reads the registered route table at test time rather than a fixed list, calling each route under every method it answers, so a route added later joins the refusal matrix, the namespace invariant and the surface test instead of being exempt
the matrix's fixed probes: an invented page path, //admin, a method a registered route does not answer on a page and on an API route, /api/invented and /api/admin/invented
a real browser session for the top-level navigation assertions: /admin signed out and as a vault owner, /settings as an administrator, and an invented page path
a process-launch harness that can start the app with SECRET_KEY unset or empty and capture the failure output
a direct SQL insert path into records and into dek_wrappers, bypassing every endpoint, for the two triggers
a database file holding a principal whose last_login_at is null, started twice, for the startup fill
a headless browser with console capture, loading a shell page and a Not Found page, for the no-console-error and icon-declaration assertions
focus: the header criterion is easy to fake by asserting CSP and HSTS on one happy-path route. The spec requires them on a shell page, a JSON endpoint, a Not Found and a Server Error, and a green test over one proves nothing about the others

the refusal fingerprint matrix is the test that cannot be faked by spot checks: one cell per session state (absent, expired, vault owner, administrator) and header state (absent, present), where every refused request has the status the Refusals table gives and matches every other refusal of the same status, API or page, on body and every header except Date. A test over one route or one session state shows nothing about the rest

without the header a refusal must be identical across all four session states, and with the header a refusal to an expired session must be identical to one to an absent session. Comparing an expired session with only a valid one, or checking status without body and headers, leaves the leak in place

a refusal must carry no Set-Cookie, no Allow, no Location and no route-set header such as Cache-Control: no-store or Referrer-Policy. Comparing status and body alone misses exactly these, and a Method Not Allowed or a trailing-slash redirect leaks through them

the method and address probes matter: a method a route does not answer and //admin must be refused as an invented address, never Method Not Allowed and never a redirect. A test that only requests unknown paths passes while the router still answers these differently

the namespace invariant must be asserted over the route map enumerated at test time: every route requiring the header is under /api/, every other route is exempt and answers only GET and HEAD, and no route answers OPTIONS. A fixed route list passes forever and misses the next route added

'no error in the browser console' covers every screen including the error pages reached by navigation, not only the happy-path shell pages. It needs a real browser load of a Not Found page with console messages captured, and a missing icon declaration on an error template passes every server-side test

the icon criterion has three halves that each fake easily: every shell page and every error page carries the declaration, the icon is fetchable with no header and no session, and /favicon.ico is refused with the status, body and headers of an invented page path. Asserting the declaration on one template proves nothing about the error pages, and adding a /favicon.ico route or exemption to quiet the console passes the fetch half while breaking the third

the exempt-route criterion must be tested against an actual exempt route and against a nearby non-exempt route under the same prefix, because the exemption is per named route and a pattern-based implementation passes the first half

the surface split must be asserted by enumerating the registered routes at test time and calling each with a session of both kinds. A route that answers something other than Not Found to the wrong kind, or that appears in neither group, has to fail the test

the Public group must be asserted over the route map enumerated at test time, against the list in publicRoutes: with no session the gate passes exactly the Public routes (with the header, for API routes) and the vault navigation pages, and refuses every other route under every method it answers. A test over the listed routes alone passes while a route added later answers without a session
an administrator's GET /api/records must return Not Found and not an empty list, asserted specifically. An empty list passes any test that only checks no other vault's rows came back

the page Not Found must be identical in a real browser for /admin signed out, /admin as a vault owner, /settings as an administrator and an invented path. A server-side comparison alone does not show that the rendered page depends on neither session nor kind
the two triggers must be asserted with a direct SQL insert, not through an endpoint. An endpoint that happens to refuse the insert for its own reasons hides whether the schema refuses it at all

the last_login_at fill must be run against a real file with a null row at app start, and a second start must change nothing, asserted against the row's value after each. A fill in a one-off migration script or one that rewrites already-set values passes a single-start test

the SECRET_KEY criterion needs a real process start attempt and inspection of the failure output for the variable name and the absence of any value. A unit test of a config loader in isolation is not the same thing

'no response body originating in the shell contains vault plaintext' cannot be checked by grepping the shell's templates, since the shell never holds plaintext to begin with. The assertion that matters is that no route wired to the shell ever receives decrypted content to render
